newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Benco jumps after diamond concession buy.
newsitem.headline: Benco jumps after diamond concession buy.

text.p: Shares in Benguela Concessions Ltd (Benco) rose on Tuesday on news it had bought all the sea diamond mining concessions belonging to its joint venture partner BHP Minerals International Exploration Inc.
By 0743 GMT Benco was up 65 cents or over 12.6 percent to 580 cents in brisk trade of 115,700 shares.
"It's up after the story in the newspaper," a dealer said, referring to a published announcement earlier.

The announcement said that Benco had bought BHP's majority stake in their joint venture, including concessions, all equipment and a vast data base of exploration results in exchange for BHP taking a 25 percent stake in Benco.
The price of the deal with BHP, a unit of Australian mining giant The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, was put at 110 million rand.
"This is a fantastic show of faith in Benco by one of the world's largest mining companies," Benco chairman John Gurney said in a statement late on Monday.

Benco said that the joint venture, formed in January 1993 for the exploration and development of marine diamond deposits off the west coast of southern Africa, had been terminated with effect from May 31.
This deal will enable Benco to continue to explore and develop the marine diamond consessions for its own account.
But one dealer said that the share's rise might be overdone.
"The concessions are not going to be mined for some years, so we still prefer ODM," he said, referring to fellow South African marine diamond firm Ocean Diamond Mining Holdings Ltd .
